learning_objective: 🎯 Master database manipulation! Learn how to extract exact information using SQL single-row functions and group large datasets using aggregate functions.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: SQL provides built-in tools for numbers. POWER(x, y) calculates x to the power of y. ROUND(n, d) rounds a number to 'd' decimal places. MOD(x, y) gives the remainder when x is divided by y.

Tools to manipulate text! UCASE()/UPPER() converts to capitals. LCASE()/LOWER() converts to small letters. LENGTH() counts the characters. SUBSTR(string, start, length) extracts a specific piece of the text.
Handle time easily. NOW() gives the current date and time. SYSDATE() is similar but evaluates at execution. YEAR(), MONTH(), and DAY() extract specific parts from a date format (YYYY-MM-DD).
These functions work on multiple rows to return a SINGLE answer. MAX() finds the highest, MIN() the lowest, AVG() the average, SUM() the total, and COUNT() counts the number of rows.

GROUP BY groups rows that have the same values into summary rows (like finding total salary per department). The HAVING clause acts like a WHERE clause, but it is strictly used to filter these grouped records!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ The School Database Hacker
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine your school has an SQL table called 'STUDENTS'. Write a mental query to find the tallest student in Class 12. It would look like: SELECT MAX(Height) FROM STUDENTS WHERE Class = 12; You just 'hacked' the data!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the difference between COUNT(*) and COUNT(column_name). COUNT(*) counts every single row including NULLs. COUNT(column_name) ignores NULL values.
📌 The WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping. The HAVING clause filters groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause has been applied.
📌 In SUBSTR(string, start, length), remember that SQL indexing starts at 1, NOT 0 like Python!
quick_recap: ⭐ Single-row functions return one result per row (e.g., LENGTH), while Multi-row functions return one result for a group of rows (e.g., SUM).
⭐ The ORDER BY clause is used to sort the result-set in ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC) order.
⭐ ROUND(15.193, 1) will output 15.2, rounding up because the next digit is 9.
